a5207.t:
Dix-huit jours après la fin des Assises Nationales, la Commission nationale, dirigée par le Docteur Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey, a procédé le lundi 10 mars 2025 à la remise officielle du rapport final des travaux au Président du Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (CNSP), Chef de l’Etat, le Général de Brigade Abdourahamane Tiani. Ce document inclut diverses recommandations, un avant-projet de la Charte de refondation, ainsi que des résolutions explicites comme celle qui propose l’élévation du Chef de l’État au rang de Général d’Armée.
Cette cérémonie solennelle s’est déroulée en présence du Premier ministre, ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, M. Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, des anciens Chefs d’Etat et anciens présidents de l’Assemblée Nationale, du président de la Cour d’Etat, des membres du Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie, des membres du Gouvernement, les chefs traditionnels et religieux et plusieurs invités.
Les assises ont ainsi préconisé une durée minimale de la transition de 5 ans, renouvelable selon les conditions sécuritaires, le programme de refondation et l’agenda de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). Elles ont également suggéré la dissolution des partis politiques ainsi que l’élaboration d’une nouvelle charte. « En mon nom personnel et au nom de l’ensemble des membres de la Commission nationale chargée des Assises Nationales, j’ai le plaisir et l’honneur de vous remettre le présent document », a dit Docteur Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey au Président du CNSP.
Peu après avoir reçu ce document final, le Président du Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie, Chef de l’Etat, a réitéré ses remerciements au Président en charge de l’organisation des travaux, qui a piloté ces assises de manière experte, avec le soutien infaillible de son équipe. « J’exprime toute ma reconnaissance et ma gratitude à tous ceux qui ont, de près ou de loin et de quelque manière que ce soit, participé à ces travaux dont aujourd’hui, nous sommes en train de recevoir les copies des mains du président de la Commission nationale qui a conduit les travaux des assises. Merci honorable ! Merci à l’ensemble du peuple nigérien qui vous a accompagné et soutenu. Gardons à l’esprit que ce n’est plus le moment des rancœurs, des divisions, d’adversités stériles. Tout ce que nous devons faire doit s’inscrire dans la défense et dans la préservation des intérêts du Niger. Le Niger, sans lequel nous n’aurons pas de raison d’être, ce Niger que nous avons le devoir de défendre au prix de nos vies. In shaa Allah, nous y parviendrons », a déclaré le Général de Brigade Abdourahamane Tiani.
À la clôture des travaux des Assises Nationales qui s’est tenue le 20 février dernier, le Chef de l’État, a offert la possibilité à ceux qui n’ont pas pu participer aux débats de le faire dans les trois semaines à venir. « Je crois que ce délai était suffisant pour que ceux qui n’ont pas pu participer au débat puissent apporter leurs contributions car, comme nous le disons et le répéterons ‘’Labou Sanni no’’, ‘’Zancen Kassa ne’’, ‘’Hala ledi non’’. Les intérêts du Niger sont au-dessus de tout regroupement, de tout individualisme et de tout clanisme. Il faut que le Niger existe pour que des intérêts particuliers subsistent ; travaillons pour l’existence de notre pays, particulièrement en ce temps difficile où nous faisons face à une insécurité. Comme nous l’avons toujours affirmé, il est de notre responsabilité de mettre fin à cette importation de l’insécurité dans notre Sahel pour qu’il soit désormais un espace de prospérité pour l’ensemble des peuples qui y vivent, plutôt qu’un espace d’insécurité. Et qui dit insécurité dit misère et pertes en vies humaines inutiles », a mentionné le Général de Brigade Abdourahamane Tiani.
Pour le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité Publique et de l’Administration du Territoire, le Général de Brigade Mohamed Toumba, l’histoire retiendra que la population, à travers la Commission Nationale chargée de conduire les travaux des Assises Nationales, a marqué le début d’un nouveau chapitre pour le pays, contribuant ainsi, comme l’a exprimé le Chef de l’État dans son discours d’ouverture des Assises nationales, ‘’à poser des fondations solides pour un avenir de stabilité politique et de progrès économique et social pour tous’’.
« L’analyse du résumé de rapport final contient, entre autres, la formulation de plusieurs recommandations par les participants aux Assises Nationales issues du diagnostic du contexte social, économique, culturel et politique de notre pays, en lien avec les cinq thématiques ayant servi de base de travail aux assises , la proposition du projet de la Charte de la refondation qui servira une fois adoptée de loi fondamentale à valeur constitutionnelle de notre pays et l’adoption de trois résolutions relatives à la durée de la transition de cinq ans modulable, l’élévation de votre excellence au grade de Général d’armée et enfin la dissolution des partis politiques et l’adoption d’une nouvelle charte des partis politiques qui prend en compte les réalités socioculturelles de notre pays », a précisé le Général Mohamed Toumba.
Fatiyatou Inoussa (ONEP)
a5207.en:
Eighteen days after the end of the National Assises (national consultations), the National Commission, headed by Dr Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey, proceeded on Monday 10 March 2025 to the official handover of the final report of the proceedings to the President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP), Head of State, Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani. This document includes various recommendations, a draft Charter of Refoundation, as well as explicit resolutions such as the one proposing the elevation of the Head of State to the rank of Army General.

This solemn ceremony took place in the presence of the Prime Minister, Minister of the Economy and Finance, Mr Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, former Heads of State and former presidents of the National Assembly, the president of the State Court, members of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland, members of the Government, traditional and religious leaders and several guests.

The assises thus recommended a minimum transition period of 5 years, renewable according to security conditions, the refoundation programme and the agenda of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES). They also suggested the dissolution of political parties as well as the drafting of a new charter. "In my own name and on behalf of all the members of the National Commission responsible for the National Assises, it is my pleasure and honour to hand you the present document," Dr Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey told the President of the CNSP.

Shortly after receiving this final document, the President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland, Head of State, reiterated his thanks to the President in charge of organising the proceedings, who steered these consultations expertly, with the unfailing support of his team. "I express all my appreciation and gratitude to all those who, closely or from afar and in whatever manner, took part in this work, copies of which we are today receiving from the hands of the president of the National Commission who led the proceedings of the assises. Thank you, honourable sir! Thanks to all the people of Niger who accompanied and supported you. Let us bear in mind that this is no longer the time for resentment, for divisions, for sterile antagonism. Everything we do must be inscribed in the defence and the preservation of the interests of Niger. Niger, without which we would have no reason to exist, this Niger that we have a duty to defend at the cost of our lives. God willing, we shall succeed," declared Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani.

At the closing of the proceedings of the National Assises, held on 20 February, the Head of State had offered those who had been unable to take part in the debates the possibility of doing so within the following three weeks. "I believe that this deadline was sufficient for those who could not take part in the debate to make their contributions because, as we say and will repeat, 'Labou Sanni no', 'Zancen Kassa ne', 'Hala ledi non' [it is a matter of the country]. The interests of Niger are above any grouping, any individualism and any clannishness. Niger must exist for particular interests to survive; let us work for the existence of our country, particularly in this difficult time in which we face insecurity. As we have always affirmed, it is our responsibility to put an end to this importation of insecurity into our Sahel so that it may henceforth be a space of prosperity for all the peoples who live there, rather than a space of insecurity. And insecurity means misery and needless loss of human life," mentioned Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani.

For the Minister of State, Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration, Brigadier General Mohamed Toumba, history will record that the population, through the National Commission charged with conducting the proceedings of the National Assises, marked the beginning of a new chapter for the country, thereby contributing, as the Head of State expressed in his opening address to the National Assises, "to laying solid foundations for a future of political stability and of economic and social progress for all."

"The analysis of the summary of the final report contains, among other things, the formulation of several recommendations by the participants in the National Assises arising from the diagnosis of the social, economic, cultural and political context of our country, in connection with the five themes that served as the basis of the assises' work; the proposal of the draft Charter of Refoundation which, once adopted, will serve as the fundamental law with constitutional force of our country; and the adoption of three resolutions relating to the adjustable five-year transition period, the elevation of Your Excellency to the rank of Army General, and finally the dissolution of political parties and the adoption of a new charter of political parties that takes into account the sociocultural realities of our country," specified General Mohamed Toumba.

Fatiyatou Inoussa (ONEP)

a5273.t:
Le chanteur qui est toujours en liberté conditionnelle pour avoir frappé la chanteuse Rihanna a été placé en état d’arrestation ce dimanche pour avoir frappé un homme en bas de son hôtel. Il est également accusé d’avoir proféré des insultes homophobes.
Chris Brown qui posait pour une photo avec des fans n’a pas du tout apprécié que l’individu lui joue un tour en se positionnant dans son dos, mimant des grimaces. Il lui aurait alors rétorqué qu’il préfèrait se comporter comme un boxeur plutôt qu’un gay. Le jeune homme agressé qui a eu le nez cassé, a affirmé vouloir porter plainte. Ce qui pourrait conduire le jeune chanteur reconnu pour ses excès de colère risque ainsi 4 ans de prison ferme étant toujours en liberté conditionnelle. Son garde du corps et lui-même ont été placés en garde à vue en attendant la suite des événements. Chris Brown s’était plusieurs fois battu depuis l’affaire Rihanna, contre de potentiels rivaux, et contre d’autres chanteurs.
a5273.en:
The singer, who is still on probation for having struck the singer Rihanna, was placed under arrest this Sunday for hitting a man outside his hotel. He is also accused of having uttered homophobic insults.

Chris Brown, who was posing for a photo with fans, did not at all appreciate the individual playing a trick on him by positioning himself behind his back, pulling faces. He reportedly retorted to him that he would rather behave like a boxer than like a gay man. The young man who was assaulted, and whose nose was broken, said he wanted to file a complaint. This could lead the young singer, known for his fits of anger, to face 4 years in prison, as he is still on probation. His bodyguard and he himself were taken into police custody pending further developments. Chris Brown had fought several times since the Rihanna affair, against potential rivals and against other singers.

a5326.t:
Muktasari:
- Washtakiwa hao wanadaiwa mwaka 2025 katika Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, kwa nia ya kulaghai walitengeneza nyaraka za uongo ambazo ni kibali cha kumiliki silaha chenye jina la Marwaan Habretsh, Maurice Kitiwe na Said Mohamed, wakati wakijua kufanya hivyo ni kinyume cha sheria.
Dar es Salaam. Upelelezi wa kesi ya kughushi vibali vya kumiliki silaha inayowakabili watu tisa wakiwemo maofisa sita wa Jeshi la Polisi, upo hatua za mwisho kukamilika.
Wakili wa Serikali, Clemence Kato, ameieleza Mahakama ya Hakimu Mkazi Kisutu, leo Alhamisi Septemba 11, 2025 ilipofikishwa mahakamani hapo kwa ajili ya kutajwa.
Wakili Kato ametoa maelezo hayo, mbele ya Hakimu Mkazi Mwandamizi, Geofrey Mhini, anayesikiliza kesi hiyo.
Washtakiwa katika kesi hiyo ni Mkaguzi wa Polisi mwenye namba PF. 19931 Fredrick Malekela(45)mkazi wa Kilwaroad; E. 4627 Sajenti Kalemwa Kaunga(54) mkazi wa Chanika; E.7855 Sajenti Edger Mlogo (54) mkazi wa Kibamba; F.1126 Sajenti Robert Titus (47) mkazi wa Kisarawe na F.5092 Sajenti John Kaposwe (46) mkazi wa Kurasini na WP 10050 Julieth Moshi (30) mkazi wa Kisarawe.
Wengine ambao sio maofisa wa jeshi hilo ni Damson Mnyilenga (59) mkulima na mkazi wa Chanika; Simon Aloyce (60) mfanyabiashara na mkazi wa Mwanza pamoja na Venrand Liberio (29) mfanyabiashara na mkazi wa Tataba.
Kato amedai kuwa kuna vitu vichache ambavyo wanamalizia na hivyo ameomba mahakama impe wiki mbili ili waweze kukamilisha upelelezi huo.
Kato baada ya kueleza hayo, hakimu Mhini alikubaliana na upande wa mashtaka na kuahirisha kesi hiyo hadi Septemba 25, 2025 itakapotajwa na washtakiwa wapo nje kwa dhamana.
Kwa mujibu wa hati ya mashtaka, washtakiwa wanakabiliwa na kesi hiyo ya jinai ya mwaka 2025, yenye mashtaka 16 ya kughushi vibali vya kumiliki silaha.
Washtakiwa kwa pamoja wanadaiwa kutenda makosa hayo, kinyume na kifungu namba 333 na 335A na kifungu 337 cha Sheria ya Kanuni ya Adhabu , Sura ya 16 iliyofanyiwa marejeo mwaka 2019.
Katika mashtaka yao, wanadaiwa kuwa vibali hivyo, vimetolea kati ya Desemba 5, 2024 hadi Aprili 4, 2025
Katika shtaka la kwanza, washtakiwa kwa pamoja wanadaiwa katika kipindi cha mwaka 2024, ndani ya Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, kwa nia ya kudanganya walitengeneza nyaraka ya uongo ambayo ni kibali cha kumiliki silaha cha Desemba 5, 2024 chenye jina la Ahmed Ally, wakati wakijua kuwa sio kweli.
Shtaka la pili hadi la 13, washtakiwa wanadaiwa katika kipindi cha mwaka 2024 ndani ya Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, walitengeneza vibali vya kumiliki silaha vyenye majina ya Ahmed Ahmed Sandrudin, Omary Abdallah, Robert Koka, Fathi Ally, Mohamed Salim, Suleman Mbewa, Mickdad Chakindo, Irfan Nafari, Gulam Abbas Najafi, Ismail Ismail na Salim Salim.
Shtaka la 14 hadi 16, washtakiwa hao wanadaiwa mwaka 2025 katika mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, kwa nia ya kulaghai walitengeneza nyaraka za uongo ambazo ni kibali cha kumiliki silaha chenye jina la Marwaan Habretsh, Maurice Kitiwe na Said Mohamed,wakati wakijua kufanya hivyo ni kinyume cha sheria.
Kwa mara ya kwanza, washtakiwa hao walifikishwa mahakamani hapo Julai 28, 2025 na kusomewa mashtaka hayo ambayo waliyakana na wapo nje kwa dhamana.
a5326.en:
Summary:
- The accused are alleged to have, in 2025 in the Dar es Salaam Region, with intent to defraud, made false documents, namely firearm ownership permits bearing the names of Marwaan Habretsh, Maurice Kitiwe and Said Mohamed, while knowing that doing so was contrary to the law.

Dar es Salaam. The investigation into the case of forging firearm ownership permits, which faces nine people including six officers of the Police Force, is in its final stages of completion.

State Attorney Clemence Kato told the Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court today, Thursday September 11, 2025, when the case was brought before that court for mention.

Attorney Kato gave that explanation before Senior Resident Magistrate Geofrey Mhini, who is hearing the case.

The accused in the case are: Police Inspector with force number PF. 19931 Fredrick Malekela (45), a resident of Kilwa Road; E. 4627 Sergeant Kalemwa Kaunga (54), a resident of Chanika; E.7855 Sergeant Edger Mlogo (54), a resident of Kibamba; F.1126 Sergeant Robert Titus (47), a resident of Kisarawe; and F.5092 Sergeant John Kaposwe (46), a resident of Kurasini; and WP 10050 Julieth Moshi (30), a resident of Kisarawe.

The others, who are not officers of that force, are Damson Mnyilenga (59), a farmer and resident of Chanika; Simon Aloyce (60), a businessman and resident of Mwanza; and Venrand Liberio (29), a businessman and resident of Tataba.

Kato claimed that there are a few items they are finalising and therefore asked the court to give him two weeks so that they can complete that investigation.

After Kato explained this, Magistrate Mhini agreed with the prosecution side and adjourned the case until September 25, 2025, when it will be mentioned, with the accused being out on bail.

According to the charge sheet, the accused face this criminal case of 2025, carrying 16 counts of forging firearm ownership permits.

The accused are jointly alleged to have committed those offences, contrary to sections 333 and 335A and section 337 of the Penal Code, Chapter 16, as revised in 2019.

In their charges, it is alleged that those permits were issued between December 5, 2024 and April 4, 2025.

In the first count, the accused are jointly alleged to have, during 2024, within the Dar es Salaam Region, with intent to deceive, made a false document, namely a firearm ownership permit of December 5, 2024 bearing the name of Ahmed Ally, while knowing it was not true.

In counts two to 13, the accused are alleged to have, during 2024 within the Dar es Salaam Region, made firearm ownership permits bearing the names of Ahmed Ahmed Sandrudin, Omary Abdallah, Robert Koka, Fathi Ally, Mohamed Salim, Suleman Mbewa, Mickdad Chakindo, Irfan Nafari, Gulam Abbas Najafi, Ismail Ismail and Salim Salim.

In counts 14 to 16, the accused are alleged to have, in 2025 in the Dar es Salaam region, with intent to defraud, made false documents, namely firearm ownership permits bearing the names of Marwaan Habretsh, Maurice Kitiwe and Said Mohamed, while knowing that doing so was contrary to the law.

The accused were first brought before that court on July 28, 2025 and had those charges read to them, which they denied, and they are out on bail.

a5524.t:
"Não nos testem no norte", advertiu o governante israelita, num momento em que Israel reúne tropas junto ao território da Faixa de Gaza, em preparação para uma provável ofensiva contra o Hamas na sequência do ataque-surpresa conduzido pelo grupo islamita palestiniano no passado dia 07 de Outubro.
Num discurso no Knesset (parlamento) israelita, Netanyahu disse igualmente que o mundo "precisa de se unir para derrotar" o Hamas, grupo considerado terrorista pela União Europeia (UE) e pelos Estados Unidos e que governa a Faixa de Gaza desde 2007.
"Esta guerra é também a vossa [comunidade internacional] guerra", afirmou na mesma intervenção, associando o Hamas ao regime nazi.
Durante a sessão parlamentar, que decorre em Jerusalém e ainda na presença de Netanyahu, foram ouvidas várias explosões próximas do edifício, sem que, até ao momento, existam informações sobre o registo de mortos ou de feridos.
A sessão do parlamento acabou por ser interrompida, embora um porta-voz parlamentar tenha dito aos meios de comunicação hebraicos que esta seria retomada logo que possível.
As sirenes antiaéreas, que normalmente anunciam a chegada de foguetes lançados de Gaza pelo movimento islamita Hamas, também soaram no centro de Israel e em Telavive, confirmou o exército israelita.
Segundo os relatos das agências internacionais, os palestinianos da Faixa de Gaza aglomeraram-se hoje em hospitais e escolas, à procura de abrigo e com pouca comida e água.
Mais de um milhão de pessoas terá fugido até ao momento das respectivas casas antes de uma esperada ofensiva terrestre israelita, que está a ser planeada por Telavive para destruir o Hamas, depois de os seus combatentes terem invadido o sul de Israel.
À medida que as reservas de alimentos, água e medicamentos do enclave palestiniano diminuem, todas as atenções se voltaram para a passagem de Rafah, entre Gaza e o Egipto, onde os camiões que transportam a ajuda humanitária aguardam há dias, enquanto os mediadores pressionam para um cessar-fogo que lhes permita a entrada em Gaza e possibilite a saída de estrangeiros.
Rafah, a única ligação de Gaza ao Egipto, foi encerrada há quase uma semana devido aos ataques aéreos israelitas.
O ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros do Egipto, Sameh Shoukry, disse que Israel "não tomou posição para abrir a passagem do lado de Gaza".
Centenas de milhares de palestinianos abrigados em instalações da ONU estão a receber menos de um litro de água por dia.
Os hospitais de Gaza alertaram para o facto de estarem à beira do colapso, com os geradores de emergência, que garantem o funcionamento de máquinas como ventiladores e incubadoras, a contarem com menos de um dia de combustível. As unidades hospitalares também relataram que as reservas de medicamentos estão quase esgotadas.
a5524.en:
“Do not test us in the north,” warned the Israeli leader, at a time when Israel is massing troops along the territory of the Gaza Strip, in preparation for a probable offensive against Hamas following the surprise attack carried out by the Palestinian Islamist group on 7 October.

In a speech to the Israeli Knesset (parliament), Netanyahu also said that the world “needs to unite to defeat” Hamas, a group considered terrorist by the European Union (EU) and the United States and which has governed the Gaza Strip since 2007.

“This war is also your [the international community’s] war,” he stated in the same address, associating Hamas with the Nazi regime.

During the parliamentary session, which is taking place in Jerusalem and still in Netanyahu’s presence, several explosions were heard near the building, without, so far, any information about dead or wounded.

The parliamentary session ended up being interrupted, although a parliamentary spokesman told Hebrew media that it would be resumed as soon as possible.

The air-raid sirens, which normally announce the arrival of rockets launched from Gaza by the Islamist movement Hamas, also sounded in central Israel and in Tel Aviv, the Israeli army confirmed.

According to reports from the international agencies, Palestinians in the Gaza Strip crowded today into hospitals and schools, looking for shelter and with little food and water.

More than a million people are said to have fled their homes so far, ahead of an expected Israeli ground offensive being planned by Tel Aviv to destroy Hamas, after its fighters invaded southern Israel.

As the Palestinian enclave’s reserves of food, water and medicines dwindle, all attention has turned to the Rafah crossing, between Gaza and Egypt, where the trucks carrying humanitarian aid have been waiting for days, while mediators press for a ceasefire that would allow them to enter Gaza and make it possible for foreigners to leave.

Rafah, Gaza’s only link to Egypt, has been closed for almost a week because of Israeli air strikes.

Egypt’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sameh Shoukry, said that Israel “has not taken a position to open the crossing on the Gaza side”.

Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians sheltering in UN facilities are receiving less than one litre of water per day.

Gaza’s hospitals have warned that they are on the brink of collapse, with the emergency generators that keep machines such as ventilators and incubators running having less than a day’s fuel left. The hospital units also reported that their reserves of medicines are almost exhausted.

a5632.t:
Leopoldino Bambo
Matola acolhe uma das viagens experimentais da locomotiva Metrobus que realizará a sua primeira viagem operacional a 1 de Fevereiro próximo. 
Com estas viagens pretende-se melhorar a operacionalização do projecto, devido à elevada afluência de passageiros esperada por conta dos resultados do último senso populacional realizado.
O início das operações da locomotiva está agendada para um de Fevereiro, a estação ferroviária será erguida no recinto da terminal de carga na Matola, e será composta por uma loja de conveniência, uma oficina automóvel com dezasseis especialidades e um parque de estacionamento para quatrocentas viaturas.
A viagem experimental da linha Maputo Matola contou com a presença do Vereador de Planeamento Territorial e Urbanização do Município da Matola, José Sambo que realçou a importância do Metrobus na melhoria do sistema de transportes de passageiros.
A Província de Inhambane prevê arrecadar mais de mil cento e trinta mil milhões de meticais de receitas no presente ano.
A indústria extractiva, agricultura, turismo e pescas são os sectores que se vão destacar na efectivação do plano traçado pelo Governo Provincial.
As polícias de Moçambique e Tanzânia assinaram um memorando de entendimento para o reforço das relações de segurança. 
Os recentes casos de ataques no norte de Cabo Delgado marcaram as conversações entre as chefias polícias dos países.
Dos atacantes mortos pela polícia moçambicana, 4 faziam parte de um grupo de malfeitores recentemente perseguidos na Tanzânia e que se refugiou, no território moçambicano.
Hienas matam e devoram ovelhas, na localidade de Ligogolo, distrito de Muembe, província do Niassa.
Nos últimos 2 meses, aqueles animais selvagens devoraram 8 ovelhas e dezanove são dadas como desaparecidas na criação de um investidor agro-pecuário sul-africano na região.
Governo moçambicano introduz a testagem da qualidade de medicamentos, na origem, para evitar a importação de fármacos sem qualidade, não registados, e até falsificados ou contra-feitos.
Para o efeito, a Ministra da Saúde lançou hoje em Maputo o projecto de inspecção pré-embarque de medicamentos, que numa primeira fase será na Índia, maior exportador de fármacos para Moçambique.
Com esta medida o produto indesejado para Moçambique será descartado ainda no país de origem, antes de se incorrer em quaisquer custos operacionais de exportação e importação.
Também será evitado o risco de circulação de medicamentos inapropriados ou contrabandeados, no destino, onde a fiscalização é ainda deficitária, pese embora o laboratório nacional de medicamentos faça a testagem. 
Actualmente a inspecção pré-embarque é feita por uma entidade privada, INTERTEK, que a faz de forma visual e documental, sem nenhuma testagem analítica da qualidade e conformidade com a certificação.
Moçambique adopta esta medida em cumprimento da recomendação da auditoria do fundo global e se suporta na experiência da Nigéria e do Gana, que já implementam a testagem pré-embarque de medicamentos na origem.
Na componente legal, já existe um despacho ministerial datado de Março de 2017, que impõe o procedimento considerado de vital importância para a protecção da saúde pública.
Baixo nível de pagamento do imposto pessoal autárquico – IPA por parte dos munícipes condiciona o desempenho do Município do Maputo na arrecadação de Receitas fiscais.
Dos pouco mais de quatro mil milhões de meticais previstos para a despesa pública de 2017, a edilidade registou um défice de arrecadação de cerca de trinta por cento, mesmo assim as autoridades municipais dão se por satisfeitas com a participação nos impostos predial e de veículo.
O Consulado Português inaugurou, em Maputo, um novo centro de pedido de vistos para Portugal. 
O Centro funciona na parte baixa da capital moçambicana.
O Centro foi inaugurado esta quarta-feira e está localizado num dos pisos do Maputo Shopping, na baixa da capital moçambicana.
Com este centro a funcionar, o Consulado Português espera ultrapassar os cerca de nove mil vistos que foram emitidos em 2017, deixando, desta forma, os moçambicanos e os cidadãos de outras nacionalidades, residentes no país, mais confortáveis para efectuar viagens para Portugal.
Universidade Pedagógica delegação da Beira regista trezentas e oitenta e nove ausências até ao terceiro dia dos exames de admissão naquela instituição do ensino superior. 
Alguns candidatos não compareceram as salas de exames e outros não apresentaram a documentação exigida.
Pragas de lagarta invasora e gafanhoto elefante destruíram mais de mil hectares de milho e arroz, na Província da Zambézia.
 O Director Provincial da Agricultura e Segurança Alimentar da Zambézia, Jabula Zibia, assegura, no entanto que, já foram mobilizados extensionistas e quantidades de insecticida para combater a praga.
Produtores de algodão abandonaram o cultivo desta cultura a favor do garimpo no distrito de Montepuez, em Cabo Delgado
O fenómeno concorre para a redução dos níveis de produção, tendo na última campanha por exemplo, baixado em mais de sessenta porcento.
a5632.en:
Leopoldino Bambo

Matola is hosting one of the trial runs of the Metrobus locomotive, which will make its first operational journey on 1 February. These trips are intended to improve the operationalisation of the project, given the high volume of passengers expected on the basis of the results of the latest population census.

The start of the locomotive's operations is scheduled for 1 February; the railway station will be built on the grounds of the cargo terminal in Matola, and will consist of a convenience store, a vehicle workshop with sixteen specialities and a car park for four hundred vehicles.

The trial run on the Maputo-Matola line was attended by the Councillor for Territorial Planning and Urbanisation of the Municipality of Matola, José Sambo, who highlighted the importance of the Metrobus in improving the passenger transport system.

Inhambane Province expects to collect more than one thousand one hundred and thirty thousand million meticais in revenue this year. The extractive industry, agriculture, tourism and fisheries are the sectors that will stand out in carrying out the plan drawn up by the Provincial Government.

The police forces of Mozambique and Tanzania have signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen security relations. The recent cases of attacks in the north of Cabo Delgado marked the talks between the two countries' police chiefs. Of the attackers killed by the Mozambican police, 4 were part of a group of criminals recently pursued in Tanzania who had taken refuge in Mozambican territory.

Hyenas are killing and devouring sheep in the locality of Ligogolo, Muembe district, Niassa province. Over the past 2 months, those wild animals have devoured 8 sheep and nineteen are reported missing from the livestock of a South African agro-livestock investor in the region.

The Mozambican government is introducing quality testing of medicines at source, to prevent the importation of substandard, unregistered and even falsified or counterfeit drugs. To that end, the Minister of Health today launched in Maputo the pre-shipment medicines inspection project, which in a first phase will be carried out in India, the largest exporter of pharmaceuticals to Mozambique.

With this measure, the product unwanted for Mozambique will be discarded in the country of origin, before incurring any operational export and import costs. It will also avoid the risk of inappropriate or smuggled medicines circulating at the destination, where inspection is still deficient, even though the national medicines laboratory carries out testing.

At present, pre-shipment inspection is carried out by a private entity, INTERTEK, which does it visually and on the documents, without any analytical testing of quality and conformity with the certification.

Mozambique is adopting this measure in compliance with the recommendation of the Global Fund audit and draws on the experience of Nigeria and Ghana, which already implement pre-shipment testing of medicines at source. On the legal side, there is already a ministerial order dated March 2017 imposing the procedure, considered of vital importance for the protection of public health.

A low level of payment of the municipal personal tax — IPA — by residents is constraining the performance of the Municipality of Maputo in collecting tax revenue. Of the slightly more than four thousand million meticais forecast for public expenditure in 2017, the municipality recorded a collection shortfall of about thirty per cent; even so, the municipal authorities declare themselves satisfied with the take from property and vehicle taxes.

The Portuguese Consulate has inaugurated in Maputo a new centre for visa applications for Portugal. The Centre operates in the lower part of the Mozambican capital. The Centre was inaugurated this Wednesday and is located on one of the floors of Maputo Shopping, in the downtown area of the capital. With this centre in operation, the Portuguese Consulate expects to exceed the roughly nine thousand visas that were issued in 2017, thereby leaving Mozambicans and citizens of other nationalities resident in the country more comfortable in making trips to Portugal.

The Pedagogical University's Beira delegation has recorded three hundred and eighty-nine absences up to the third day of the entrance examinations at that higher education institution. Some candidates did not turn up in the examination rooms and others did not present the required documentation.

Infestations of invasive caterpillar and elephant grasshopper have destroyed more than one thousand hectares of maize and rice in Zambezia Province. The Provincial Director of Agriculture and Food Security of Zambezia, Jabula Zibia, nevertheless assures that extension workers and quantities of insecticide have already been mobilised to combat the pest.

Cotton producers have abandoned the cultivation of that crop in favour of artisanal mining in Montepuez district, Cabo Delgado. The phenomenon contributes to the reduction of production levels, with the last campaign, for example, falling by more than sixty per cent.

a5795.t:
Mali-Espagne : une coopération exemplaire et stratégique !
Aujourd'hui, on peut dire sans risque de se tromper que la coopération entre la République du Mali et le Royaume d'Espagne se porte bien et même à merveille. Cette coopération a été davantage renforcée depuis l'arrivée de l'ambassadeur Antonio Guillen Hidalgo en mars 2024. Et ce n'est pas pour rien que ce diplomate chevronné est considéré comme "le plus Malien des Espagnols".
Du coup, la coopération marche bien à travers l'Agence espagnole de coopération, qui joue sa partition. Et comme l'a si bien dit l'ambassadeur Antonio Guillen Hidalgo, le Royaume d'Espagne est présent au Mali à travers plusieurs projets, notamment dans les domaines du développement rural, de la santé, de la sécurité alimentaire, de la formation des jeunes, de l'accès à l'eau potable. Sans oublier le soutien aux femmes.
De plus en plus, cette coopération s'étend dans les domaines de la culture et du sport à l'image du Festival Hola Bamako dont la 7e édition s'est tenue avec succès tout comme la 1re édition du Hola Karaté.
Pour le diplomate espagnol, le Mali est considéré par l'Espagne comme un pays prioritaire dans son aide au développement. Raison pour laquelle, le budget de l'AECID a été doublé tout comme l'aide aux pays du Sahel qui va connaitre une nette amélioration. Cela dans le cadre de la stratégie Espagne-Afrique 2025-2028. "Depuis 2008, l'Espagne s'est toujours engagée envers et contre tout aux côtés du peuple malien. Et nous espérons continuer à écrire le livre de l'histoire de nos relations pendant de nombreuses années à venir". Parole de l'ambassadeur Antonio Guillen Hidalgo.
A la réception de la Fête nationale d'Espagne, le 11 octobre 2024, le ministre des Affaires étrangères et de la Coopération internationale, Abdoulaye Diop, se félicitait de la qualité des relations bilatérales entre les deux pays et l'approche lucide et constructive de l'Espagne sur la situation au Mali et au Sahel.
"Le gouvernement attache une importance particulière à l'objectivité dans la coopération avec nos partenaires afin que les relations soient fondées sur les principes constitutionnels qui guident l'action publique au Mali. A cet effet, je reconnais et j'apprécie l'attachement de nos deux pays au respect de l'unité nationale et de l'intégrité territoire des Etats. Je salue par ailleurs à sa juste valeur l'approche respectueuse et lucide de l'Espagne sur la situation au Mali et au Sahel.
Pour en revenir aux liens entre le Mali et l'Espagne, je note, pour m'en féliciter, notre convergence de vue concernant des questions d'importance stratégique telles que la paix et la sécurité internationales particulièrement la lutte contre le terrorisme y compris au Sahel ainsi que la bonne gouvernance", avait déclaré le ministre Diop.
Le 12 juin 2025, l'ambassadeur Antonio Guillen Hidalgo a procédé à la remise d'un chèque géant de 3 millions d'euros, soit près de 2 milliards de F CFA au Programme alimentaire mondial (Pam) pour appui au Commissariat à la sécurité alimentaire (CSA). C'est un don du Royaume d'Espagne à travers l'Agence espagnole de coopération.
"Je vous remercie pour avoir l'opportunité d'annoncer l'engagement du gouvernement espagnol, en faveur de la sécurité alimentaire au Sahel et au Mali en particulier.
J'ai aussi le plaisir de vous communiquer que l'Agence espagnole de coopération a octroyé 3 millions d'euros au Pam pour appui au CSA. Au total, la prévision d'aide humanitaire de l'Espagne au Mali en 2025 sera de 7 millions d'euros environ. 
Cette contribution, l'Espagne contribue à faire face à la crise alimentaire dans un moment où le nombre de personnes en situation d'insécurité alimentaire augmente en particulier au Sahel, en Afrique. J'espère que la contribution espagnole sera un soulagement pour les populations.
L'Espagne soutient le CSA dans sa volonté de lutter contre la faim extrême au Mali. Nous sommes conscients de la situation urgente et alarmante à laquelle le pays est confronté. Et nous sommes très satisfaits de travailler avec le Commissariat à la sécurité alimentaire. Donc, les résultats de notre appui sont toujours visibles et positifs", a souligné le diplomate espagnol lors de la remise du chèque.
Avant de préciser que "la Coopération espagnole essaie aussi d'apporter ses contributions pour améliorer la situation avec la construction d'infrastructures d'irrigation et avec l'approbation d'appui alimentaire aux déplacés internes et migrants dans le cadre d'autres interventions".
Pour le ministre-commissaire à la sécurité alimentaire, Redouwane Ag Mohamed Ali, la générosité du Royaume d'Espagne envers le Mali ne s'est jamais démentie et elle vient à nouveau de se manifester avec ce don de 3 millions d'euros en faveur des populations maliennes nécessiteuses. "Il est aujourd'hui une réalité irréfutable que le Royaume d'Espagne s'illustre comme un partenaire fiable, toujours disponible à accompagner le Mali particulièrement dans les moments difficiles.
Avec ce nouveau financement, l'Espagne réitère son engagement à accompagner le Mali dans la préservation de sa souveraineté alimentaire à travers le renforcement de la capacité de résilience des communautés vulnéraires.
Ce geste de solidarité et d'amitié vient à point nommé soutenir la vision de Son Excellence le général d'Armée Assimi Goïta, qui place la sécurité alimentaire au premier rang des priorités nationales et veut qu'aucun malien ne soit laissé de côté", a déclaré Redouwane Ag Mohamed Ali.   
Le 5 novembre 2024, l'ambassadeur d'Espagne au Mali Antonio Guillen Hidalgo a remis des maquettes des mosquées de Djenné, Sidi Yaya de Tombouctou et le Marché rose de Bamako à l'Ecole supérieure d'ingénierie, d'architecture et d'urbanisme (Esiau). La remise s'est déroulée dans l'enceinte de ladite école en présence des étudiants et formateurs de cet établissement.
En remettant ces trois maquettes à l'Esiau, le diplomate espagnol précisait que ce geste s'inscrit dans le cadre du renforcement des relations entre son pays et le Mali mais plus particulièrement avec l'Esiau qu'il a qualifiée de l'une des meilleures écoles du Mali. Il a salué le travail abattu par la dynamique équipe de l'établissement avec à sa tête son directeur général Abdoulaye Déyogo.
La participation du Premier ministre, le général de division Abdoulaye Maïga à la 4e Conférence internationale sur le financement du développement  du 30 juin au 3 juillet 2025 à Séville, en Espagne, est l'un des points positifs de la coopération entre les deux pays. 
Cette visite s'inscrivait dans une dynamique diplomatique active, contredisant les accusations d'isolement du Mali sur la scène internationale. Elle était aussi l'occasion d'une communion diplomatique majeure, porteur d'espoir pour l'économie malienne avec les Maliens vivant en Espagne. Cette présence diplomatique de haut niveau rappelle aux expatriés que le Mali les regarde, les écoute et souhaite travailler avec eux.
A travers cette visite le général Abdoulaye Maïga, le Mali réaffirmait sa place sur la scène internationale et prouvait, une fois encore, que sa souveraineté ne signifie ni isolement ni repli. Au contraire, Bamako a choisi d'ouvrir de nouveaux espaces de coopération, fondés sur le respect mutuel et les intérêts partagés.
Et du 29 septembre au 1er octobre 2025, ce fut le tour du ministre en charge de la Culture, de l'Artisanat et du Tourisme, Mamou Daffé de participer aux travaux de la Conférence mondiale sur les politiques culturelles et le développement durable (Mondiacult 2025), tenus à Barcelone en Espagne.
Notons que Mondiacult est la plus grande conférence mondiale sur les politiques culturelles. L'édition 2025 a rassemblé des milliers de participants afin de définir l'Agenda mondial de la culture pour les années à venir. Les discussions ont porté sur six thèmes et deux domaines d'intérêt, représentant les principaux défis et opportunités pour l'avenir de la culture.
Mondiacult est également une plateforme de plaidoyer majeure. Avec la conclusion du Programme de développement durable à l'horizon 2030 en vue, la Conférence de l'Unesco 2025 fut un moment décisif pour construire un consensus et un élan pour établir la culture comme un objectif "à part entière" au sein de la prochaine stratégie de développement des Nations Unies.
Profitant de son séjour, le ministre Mamou Daffé a eu des échanges fructueux avec les certains responsables de la culture et de l'Espagne. Il a rencontré le mercredi 1er octobre 2025 son homologue espagnol, Ernest Urtasun, en présence de l'ambassadeur du Mali auprès de l'Unesco, Amadou Opa Thiam et sa délégation.
Les échanges ont porté sur le renforcement de la coopération entre le Mali et l'Espagne dans le domaine de la culture. Le ministre espagnol a salué la participation du Mali à Mondiacult 2025. Les deux ministres ont convenu de se retrouver prochainement à l'occasion de la Journée du Mali à Madrid pour échanger davantage sur le renforcement du pont culturel entre leurs pays. La rencontre s'est terminée par un échange de cadeaux, gage de la bonne santé des relations culturelles entre le Mali et l'Espagne.
Le ministre Daffé a ensuite rencontré la directrice générale de l'Unesco, Mme Audrey Azoulay. Selon Mme Azoulay, "le Mali est une source d'inspiration pour elle et pour le monde". Elle a émis le souhait de visiter très prochainement Tombouctou à l'occasion du Forum mondial des civilisations prévu en décembre 2025. Le ministre a félicité la directrice générale pour la qualité de l'organisation de Mondiacult 2025 à Barcelone.
                                                                                  
El Hadj A.B. HAIDARA
a5795.en:
Mali-Spain: an exemplary and strategic cooperation!

Today, one can say without fear of error that cooperation between the Republic of Mali and the Kingdom of Spain is doing well, indeed marvellously. This cooperation has been further strengthened since the arrival of Ambassador Antonio Guillen Hidalgo in March 2024. And it is not for nothing that this seasoned diplomat is regarded as "the most Malian of Spaniards".

As a result, the cooperation is working well through the Spanish Cooperation Agency, which is playing its part. And as Ambassador Antonio Guillen Hidalgo so aptly put it, the Kingdom of Spain is present in Mali through several projects, notably in the areas of rural development, health, food security, youth training and access to drinking water. Not forgetting support for women.

Increasingly, this cooperation is extending into culture and sport, as illustrated by the Hola Bamako Festival, whose 7th edition was held successfully, as was the 1st edition of Hola Karate.

For the Spanish diplomat, Mali is considered by Spain to be a priority country in its development aid. That is why the AECID budget has been doubled, as has aid to the Sahel countries, which will see a clear improvement. This falls within the framework of the Spain-Africa strategy 2025-2028. "Since 2008, Spain has always remained committed, against all odds, alongside the Malian people. And we hope to continue writing the book of the history of our relations for many years to come." Words of Ambassador Antonio Guillen Hidalgo.

At the reception for Spain's National Day, on 11 October 2024, the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, welcomed the quality of bilateral relations between the two countries and Spain's clear-sighted and constructive approach to the situation in Mali and the Sahel.

"The government attaches particular importance to objectivity in cooperation with our partners so that relations are founded on the constitutional principles that guide public action in Mali. To that end, I recognise and appreciate the attachment of our two countries to respect for the national unity and territorial integrity of States. I also salute at its true value Spain's respectful and clear-sighted approach to the situation in Mali and the Sahel.

To return to the ties between Mali and Spain, I note with satisfaction our convergence of views on questions of strategic importance such as international peace and security, particularly the fight against terrorism including in the Sahel, as well as good governance," Minister Diop had declared.

On 12 June 2025, Ambassador Antonio Guillen Hidalgo handed over a giant cheque for 3 million euros, nearly 2 billion CFA francs, to the World Food Programme (WFP) in support of the Food Security Commission (CSA). It is a donation from the Kingdom of Spain through the Spanish Cooperation Agency.

"I thank you for the opportunity to announce the Spanish government's commitment to food security in the Sahel and in Mali in particular.

I am also pleased to inform you that the Spanish Cooperation Agency has granted 3 million euros to the WFP in support of the CSA. In total, Spain's projected humanitarian aid to Mali in 2025 will be approximately 7 million euros.

With this contribution, Spain is helping to confront the food crisis at a time when the number of people in a situation of food insecurity is rising, particularly in the Sahel, in Africa. I hope the Spanish contribution will be a relief for the populations.

Spain supports the CSA in its determination to fight extreme hunger in Mali. We are aware of the urgent and alarming situation the country faces. And we are very pleased to work with the Food Security Commission. So the results of our support are always visible and positive," the Spanish diplomat stressed at the cheque handover.

Before specifying that "Spanish Cooperation is also trying to make its contributions to improve the situation with the construction of irrigation infrastructure and with the approval of food support for internally displaced persons and migrants within the framework of other interventions".

For the Minister-Commissioner for Food Security, Redouwane Ag Mohamed Ali, the generosity of the Kingdom of Spain towards Mali has never wavered and has just been demonstrated once again with this donation of 3 million euros for needy Malian populations. "It is today an irrefutable reality that the Kingdom of Spain stands out as a reliable partner, always available to accompany Mali, particularly in difficult times.

With this new funding, Spain reaffirms its commitment to accompany Mali in preserving its food sovereignty through strengthening the resilience capacity of vulnerable communities.

This gesture of solidarity and friendship comes at just the right moment to support the vision of His Excellency Army General Assimi Goita, who places food security at the top of national priorities and wants no Malian to be left behind," declared Redouwane Ag Mohamed Ali.

On 5 November 2024, the Spanish Ambassador to Mali Antonio Guillen Hidalgo presented models of the mosques of Djenne and Sidi Yahya of Timbuktu and of the Pink Market of Bamako to the Higher School of Engineering, Architecture and Urban Planning (Esiau). The handover took place on the school's premises in the presence of students and instructors of the institution.

In handing over these three models to Esiau, the Spanish diplomat specified that this gesture forms part of the strengthening of relations between his country and Mali, but more particularly with Esiau, which he described as one of the best schools in Mali. He praised the work accomplished by the institution's dynamic team led by its director general Abdoulaye Deyogo.

The participation of the Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maiga, in the 4th International Conference on Financing for Development from 30 June to 3 July 2025 in Seville, Spain, is one of the positive points of the cooperation between the two countries.

This visit was part of an active diplomatic dynamic, contradicting accusations that Mali is isolated on the international stage. It was also the occasion for a major diplomatic communion, carrying hope for the Malian economy with Malians living in Spain. This high-level diplomatic presence reminds expatriates that Mali sees them, hears them and wishes to work with them.

Through this visit by General Abdoulaye Maiga, Mali reaffirmed its place on the international stage and proved once again that its sovereignty means neither isolation nor withdrawal. On the contrary, Bamako has chosen to open new spaces of cooperation, founded on mutual respect and shared interests.

And from 29 September to 1 October 2025, it was the turn of the Minister in charge of Culture, Handicrafts and Tourism, Mamou Daffe, to take part in the proceedings of the World Conference on Cultural Policies and Sustainable Development (Mondiacult 2025), held in Barcelona, Spain.

Note that Mondiacult is the largest world conference on cultural policies. The 2025 edition brought together thousands of participants in order to define the Global Agenda for Culture for the years to come. Discussions covered six themes and two areas of interest, representing the main challenges and opportunities for the future of culture.

Mondiacult is also a major advocacy platform. With the conclusion of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development in sight, the 2025 UNESCO Conference was a decisive moment for building consensus and momentum to establish culture as a goal "in its own right" within the United Nations' next development strategy.

Taking advantage of his stay, Minister Mamou Daffe held fruitful exchanges with certain officials of culture and of Spain. On Wednesday 1 October 2025 he met his Spanish counterpart, Ernest Urtasun, in the presence of Mali's ambassador to UNESCO, Amadou Opa Thiam, and his delegation.

The exchanges focused on strengthening cooperation between Mali and Spain in the field of culture. The Spanish minister praised Mali's participation in Mondiacult 2025. The two ministers agreed to meet again soon on the occasion of Mali Day in Madrid to discuss further the strengthening of the cultural bridge between their countries. The meeting ended with an exchange of gifts, a token of the good health of cultural relations between Mali and Spain.

Minister Daffe then met the Director-General of UNESCO, Ms Audrey Azoulay. According to Ms Azoulay, "Mali is a source of inspiration for her and for the world". She expressed the wish to visit Timbuktu very soon on the occasion of the World Forum of Civilisations planned for December 2025. The minister congratulated the Director-General on the quality of the organisation of Mondiacult 2025 in Barcelona.

El Hadj A.B. HAIDARA

a5886.t:
Findings of a recent Afrobarometer survey show that Malawians are struggling to access public health services with 81 percent of respondents who visited public health facilities stating that they found no medicines.
The survey results were released on Friday and further show that among citizens who visited a public clinic or hospital in the past 12 months, 62 percent said it was “difficult” or “very difficult” to access the services they needed.
“Many others report high costs that prevented them from getting needed care [69 percent], absent medical personnel [50 percent] and facilities in poor condition [46 percent],” reads the survey report.
The report further showed that only four percent of the respondents said they had some form of medical aid coverage to help them pay medical bills if they get sick while 58 percent of them relied on private health insurance schemes.
Reacting to the findings in an interview yesterday, Parliamentary Committee on Health chairperson Matthews Ngwale said the results are a true reflection of the situation on the ground.
He said Malawi has not achieved its target to construct 900 health posts while healthcare workers and medicines are also inadequate in public health facilities.
The survey was conducted in August 2024 with a sample size of 1 200 respondents. Ironically, the United States Agency for International Development (USAid), one of the key financiers of healthcare initiatives, suspended its aid in January this year, meaning that the situation could be worse if the survey was conducted now.
Ngwale said the health sector relies heavily on donors, but the withdrawal of USAid support should compel government to implement the national health financing strategy which provides ways of scaling up domestic resource mobilisation.
“We need to make sure that some of the drugs should be purchased by ourselves, otherwise depending on donors for our healthcare will not take us far,” he said.
In separate interviews yesterday, Physician Assistants Union of Malawi president Solomon Chomba and Amref Health Africa in Malawi country director Hester Nyasulu called on the government to introduce levies to finance the health sector.
To fill the funding gap, Chomba said the government could establish national health insurance for people that can afford but impose levies on commodities that leave people at risk of non-communicable diseases to help cover financing gaps in the public health sector.
On his part, Nyasulu said people also need to be empowered to report their complaints to hospital ombudspersons so that some of the challenges are dealt with at community level.
In the 2025/26 National Budget, K764.4 billion was allocated to the health sector, up from K729.47 billion in the previous financial year. Out of the amount, K63 billion was for procurement of medicines and laboratory items, but the Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health said in March that K138 billion was required.
According to the 2024 Annual Economic Report, 55 percent of the country’s health expenditure comes from development partners while the government contributes 24 percent and the remaining 21 percent comprising health insurance and out-of-pocket expenditures.
Under the Health Sector Strategic Plan III covering the period 2023-2030, Malawi targets to improve access to health services by increasing the percentage of health facilities providing minimum quality of care standards from 39 percent in 2019 to 75 percent in 2030.

a5917.t:
« Le Royaume du Maroc ne peut que se réjouir de cet accord. Mais, en même temps, sous la conduite de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, Président du Comité Al-Qods, le Maroc espère, en premier lieu, que cet accord sera mis en œuvre et respecté par toutes les parties », a déclaré le ministre des Affaires étrangères, appréciant le cessez-le-feu signé entre Israël et le Hamas.
Le Maroc a salué la récente annonce d’un cessez-le-feu entre le Hamas et Israël, qui doit entrer en vigueur dimanche, et a exprimé l’espoir que l’accord sera effectivement mis en œuvre et conduira à des résultats tangibles sur le terrain.
Le ministre marocain des Affaires étrangères, Nasser Bourita, a souligné vendredi l’importance de cette évolution qui, selon lui, s’inscrit dans la vision de paix du roi Mohammed VI. Il a réitéré la position constante du Maroc sur la nécessité urgente de mettre fin à la violence et de donner la priorité à la protection des civils.
« Dans de nombreuses interventions depuis le déclenchement de la crise, Sa Majesté a souligné que la priorité urgente est d’instaurer un cessez-le-feu . Sa Majesté a également précisé dans de multiples déclarations que ce cessez-le-feu doit être permanent, contrôlable et conduire à une voie durable », a déclaré M. Bourita.
Il a souligné que le cessez-le-feu pourrait apporter plusieurs avantages cruciaux, notamment mettre un terme aux massacres et aux destructions et préserver des vies humaines. Il a ajouté qu’il faciliterait un plus grand flux d’aide humanitaire, dont le peuple palestinien a cruellement besoin.
Bourita a ajouté que l’accord permettrait de protéger les civils, notamment par la libération de prisonniers et d’otages, et de garantir que les civils ne « supportent pas le coût de ces agressions ».
« Le Royaume du Maroc ne peut que se réjouir de cet accord. Mais, en même temps, sous la conduite de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, Président du Comité Al-Qods, le Maroc espère, en premier lieu, que cet accord sera mis en œuvre et respecté par toutes les parties », a déclaré le ministre des Affaires étrangères.
Il a ajouté que le Maroc espère que l’accord de cessez-le-feu conduira à la reconstruction de Gaza et soutiendra les familles déplacées, le décrivant comme un « élément clé pour donner de la crédibilité à cet accord ».
M. Bourita a également exprimé l’espoir de Rabat de voir le cessez-le-feu ouvrir la voie à un processus de paix durable au Moyen-Orient. Il a réitéré l’appel du roi Mohammed VI à une solution à deux États, qui comprend la création d’un État palestinien indépendant avec Jérusalem-Est comme capitale.
« Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI a réitéré à plusieurs reprises qu’il n’est plus viable de continuer à gérer les crises au Moyen-Orient sans s’attaquer à leurs causes profondes. Il ne s’agit pas de cesser le feu pour mettre fin à une crise, pour ensuite attendre la suivante », a souligné M. Bourita.
Il a expliqué qu’il existe aujourd’hui une opportunité de s’appuyer sur cet accord et de lancer un processus politique pour une paix permanente et globale au Moyen-Orient dans le cadre d’une solution à deux États.
MK/ac/Sf/APA
a5917.en:
“The Kingdom of Morocco can only welcome this agreement. But at the same time, under the leadership of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, Morocco hopes, first and foremost, that this agreement will be implemented and respected by all parties,” said the Minister of Foreign Affairs, welcoming the ceasefire signed between Israel and Hamas.
Morocco welcomed the recent announcement of a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel, due to take effect on Sunday, and expressed the hope that the agreement will be effectively implemented and lead to tangible results on the ground.
The Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs, Nasser Bourita, stressed on Friday the importance of this development, which, in his view, is in line with King Mohammed VI's vision of peace. He reiterated Morocco's constant position on the urgent need to end the violence and to give priority to the protection of civilians.
“In many statements since the outbreak of the crisis, His Majesty has stressed that the urgent priority is to establish a ceasefire. His Majesty has also made clear in multiple declarations that this ceasefire must be permanent, monitorable and lead to a lasting path,” said Mr Bourita.
He stressed that the ceasefire could bring several crucial benefits, notably putting an end to the killings and destruction and saving human lives. He added that it would facilitate a greater flow of humanitarian aid, which the Palestinian people badly need.
Bourita added that the agreement would make it possible to protect civilians, notably through the release of prisoners and hostages, and to ensure that civilians do not “bear the cost of these aggressions”.
“The Kingdom of Morocco can only welcome this agreement. But at the same time, under the leadership of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, Morocco hopes, first and foremost, that this agreement will be implemented and respected by all parties,” said the Minister of Foreign Affairs.
He added that Morocco hopes the ceasefire agreement will lead to the reconstruction of Gaza and support displaced families, describing this as a “key element in giving credibility to this agreement”.
Mr Bourita also expressed Rabat's hope that the ceasefire will open the way to a lasting peace process in the Middle East. He reiterated King Mohammed VI's call for a two-State solution, which includes the creation of an independent Palestinian State with East Jerusalem as its capital.
“His Majesty King Mohammed VI has repeatedly reiterated that it is no longer viable to continue managing crises in the Middle East without addressing their root causes. It is not a matter of ceasing fire to end one crisis and then waiting for the next,” Mr Bourita emphasised.
He explained that there is today an opportunity to build on this agreement and to launch a political process for a permanent and comprehensive peace in the Middle East within the framework of a two-State solution.
MK/ac/Sf/APA

a6008.t:
The United States has announced the suspension of several development aid programmes in Africa, triggering mixed reactions across the continent.
Since his return to the White House, Donald Trump has decided to suspend multiple U.S. development aid programmes targeting African nations.
The move has sparked contrasting responses as crucial projects are now left in limbo.
Senegal: $500 Million Funding Frozen
In Senegal, Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko, revealed that a $500 million; funding package from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) has been suspended. The initiative, known as the “Senegal Power Compact,” was set to span five years.
In a statement broadcast by the news website Seneweb, Sonko remarked: “We cannot continue to rely on foreign aid. The day before yesterday, the new U.S. President announced a three-year suspension of all American development aid to poor countries, pending further review.”
South Africa: Land Reform Sparks Diplomatic Tensions
In South Africa, Washington’s decision comes amid an already tense political climate. Donald Trump has threatened to cut funding in response to a new land expropriation law. “South Africa is seizing land and treating certain groups of people VERY BADLY,” he declared.
President Cyril Ramaphosa sharply refuted these claims, emphasizing that the legislation is a constitutional legal process designed to ensure equitable land access. “We remain a constitutional democracy firmly anchored in the rule of law,” he stated.
Botswana: Concerns Over HIV/AIDS Fight
In Botswana, the suspension of the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) has raised alarm in the healthcare sector. Since 2003, the country has received over one billion pulas (approximately €70 million) to combat HIV/AIDS.
Dr. Christopher Nyanga underscored the programme’s critical role in making Botswana one of the first nations to achieve UNAIDS’ 95-95-95 targets.
Although the Ministry of Health has assured that access to antiretroviral drugs remains unaffected, several local organizations have already been instructed to halt operations. The Government of Botswana is planning discussions with the U.S. embassy to sustain the affected services.
A Shift in U.S.-Africa Relations?
The sweeping suspension of U.S. aid programmes across Africa marks a turning point in U.S.-Africa relations. While some view this as an opportunity for African nations to reduce dependency on foreign aid, others fear immediate repercussions on critical sectors such as energy, healthcare and agriculture
FSS/ac/lb/gik/APA

a6225.t:
Muktasari:
- WHO itapunguza matumizi ya mishahara kwa asilimia 25.
Dar es Salaam. Wakati Shirika la Afya Duniani (WHO) likipunguza idara zake kutoka 76 hadi 34 na gharama za wafanyakazi kwa asilimia 25 baada ya ufadhili kupungua, Tanzania imeanza kujipanga kukabiliana na hatua hiyo.
WHO imechukua hatua hiyo ikiwa takribani miezi minne baada ya Marekani kutangaza kujiondoa katika shirika hilo na kusitisha ufadhili wake.
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa WHO, Dk Tedros Ghebreyesus, katika hotuba ya ufunguzi wa mkutano wa 42 wa Kamati ya Mipango, Bajeti na Utawala ya Bodi ya Utendaji ya shirika hilo uliofanyika Mei 14, 2025, alisema kukosa ufadhili wa Marekani na kupungua kwa misaada rasmi ya maendeleo kutoka kwa baadhi ya nchi nyingine, kunasababisha pengo la mishahara kwa kipindi kijacho cha miaka miwili (2026–2027), la zaidi ya Dola za Marekani 500 milioni.
“Ukweli mchungu ni kwamba tunahitaji kupunguza matumizi ya mishahara kwa asilimia 25. Hii haimaanishi kuwa tutapunguza asilimia 25 ya wafanyakazi katika shirika lote.
“Lakini tusijidanganye; tunawaaga idadi kubwa ya wafanyakazi walio na uzoefu, uwezo na kujitolea kwa kiwango cha juu. Hii ina maana kuwa taaluma zinakatizwa na maisha kuvurugika,” alisema.
Alisema ili kuwasaidia wafanyakazi katika kipindi hicho kigumu, wameanzisha mifumo ya msaada na kujikita kusaidia katika afya ya akili na ustawi wao.
“Tunatarajia kupunguzwa wafanyakazi wengi kutatokea makao makuu, ingawa ofisi za kanda pia zitaathirika kwa viwango tofauti,” alisema.
Alisema kazi ya kuweka vipaumbele imechangia kuandaliwa kwa muundo mpya wa makao makuu, ambao aliutangaza mwezi uliopita unaopunguza idadi ya viongozi wakuu kutoka 14 hadi 7 na idadi ya idara kutoka 76 hadi 34.
“Ofisi za kanda zinakamilisha mipango yao ambayo inaendana na makao makuu,” alisema.
Wadau wa masuala ya afya nchini, wamesema kujiondoa kwa Marekani WHO ni pigo kubwa kwa mataifa yanayoendelea, ikiwamo Tanzania na nchi maskini.
Rais wa Chama cha Madaktari Tanzania (MAT), Dk Mugisha Nkoronko amesema suala hilo lilitarajiwa kutokea kutokana na mwenendo wa uchangiaji WHO unaofanywa na nchi wanachama.
Amesema mchangiaji mkubwa alikuwa Marekani kwa kipindi kirefu, akifuatiwa na mashirika mengine ya China, nchi za Ulaya na Japan.
Kujitoa imechangia kupungua kwa uendeshaji wa shirika, hivyo wamefanya uamuzi kuona wanawezaje kufanya kazi kwa hali ilivyo.
"Shirika litaweza kujiendesha bila kutegemea michango mingi, litaweza kufikiri vyanzo vipya vya mapato kuchangia shughuli zake bila kukwama,” amesema na kuongeza:
"Tunajua watu wamepoteza ajira, sijajua Watanzania wangapi walikuwapo kwenye orodha ya ajira na wangapi watakuwa wameathirika kwa kupunguza kazi. Lakini pia kuna miradi iliyoendeshwa na WHO itaathirika kwa namna moja ama nyingine au kutotimiza miradi na matokeo yaliyotarajiwa kwa wanufaika wa ufadhili huo. Zipo athari lakini kwa kiasi kikubwa wamepunguza gharama za uendeshaji." Mwenyekiti wa Chama cha watoa huduma za afya binafsi Tanzania (Aphfta), Dk Egina Makwabe amesema Marekani inachangia asilimia 30 ya bajeti ya WHO.
“Ukiangalia upande wa chanjo pale Gavi (Shirika la kimataifa linalozalisha chanjo) ule mpango wa kutoa chanjo kwa nchi maskini Marekani ndiyo ilikuwa mchangiaji mkubwa,” amesema.
Inachofanya Tanzania
Serikali ya Tanzania imesema ina akiba ya kutosha ya dawa na chanjo lakini inakuja na mikakati mipya.
"Hatuna changamoto ya ARV, hali yetu ya dawa ni nzuri na inatupeleka mpaka Juni 2026. Itakaposomwa bajeti ya Wizara (Afya) utasikia mipango ya Serikali," amesema Mfamasia Mkuu wa Serikali, Daudi Msasi alipozungumza na Mwananchi kuhusu mikakati iliyopo.
Uamuzi wa Trump
Rais Donald Trump wa Marekani Januari 20, 2025 alitia saini amri ya kiutendaji kujiondoa WHO, shirika lililoanzishwa mwaka 1948 likiwa na nchi wanachama 193. Marekani ilikuwa miongoni mwa waasisi.
Trump katika amri hiyo alisema Marekani itasitisha kutoa fedha, usaidizi au rasilimali za Serikali ya Marekani kwa WHO.
Taifa hilo limekuwa likitoa fedha, nyingi na watalaamu wa afya kwa kutumia taasisi zake za Serikali.
Kwa mujibu wa takwimu za WHO, Marekani katika kipindi cha mwaka 2022 hadi 2023 imetoa Sh3.25 trilioni.
Taifa hilo limekuwa likitoa wataalamu na ujuzi kupitia taasisi zake kama vile idara ya afya na huduma za binadamu, Kituo cha Kudhibiti Maradhi cha Marekani (CDC), Shirika la Marekani la Maendeleo ya Kimataifa (USAID), Shirika la Kulinda Mazingira la Marekani (EPA) na Mfuko wa Dharura wa Rais wa Marekani wa Kupambana na (PEPFAR).
Wachangiaji wengine wakubwa wa WHO kwa mwaka 2022-2023 ni Ujerumani Sh2.16 trilioni, Gates Foundation (Sh2.10 trilioni), Gavi (Sh1.21 trilioni), Kamisheni ya Ulaya (Sh1.18 trilioni), Uingereza na Northern Ireland (Sh1 trilioni).
Wengine ni Canada (Sh516.46 bilioni), Rotary International (Sh448.1 bilioni), Japan (Sh422.79 bilioni) na Ufaransa (Sh407.6 bilioni).
Awali, Marekani ilipendekeza kujiondoa kutoka WHO mwaka 2020 kwa sababu ya shirika hilo kushughulikia vibaya janga la Uviko-19 lililoibuka kutoka Wuhan, China na shida nyingine za kiafya duniani.
Trump katika muhula wake wa kwanza wa Urais, aliilalamikia WHO kushindwa kupitisha mageuzi yanayohitajika haraka na kutokuwa na uwezo wa kuonyesha uhuru kutoka kwa ushawishi usiofaa wa kisiasa wa nchi wanachama wa shirika hilo.
"WHO inaendelea kudai malipo yenye kutaabisha isivyo haki kutoka Marekani, mbali na uwiano na malipo yaliyotathiminiwa ya nchi nyingine. China yenye idadi ya watu bilioni 1.4 ina asilimia 300 ya wakazi wa Marekani, lakini inachangia karibu chini ya asilimia 90 ya WHO," alisema Trump.
Alisema Marekani inakusudia kujiondoa kutoka WHO ambapo barua ya kujitoa kwa Katibu Mkuu wa Umoja wa Mataifa iliyotiwa saini Januari 20, 2021 ilibatilisha ombi la Marekani la Julai 6, 2020.
Rais Trump kwa amri ya Jaruari, 2025 amesema Marekani itasitisha kutoa fedha, usaidizi au rasilimali za Serikali ya Marekani kwa WHO.
Ameamuru kuwarejesha nyumbani na kuwapa kazi upya wafanyakazi wa Serikali ya Marekani au wakandarasi wanaofanya kazi katika nafasi yoyote WHO.
Amesema Serikali ya Marekani itatafuta washirika wa kimataifa wanaoaminika na wenye uwazi ili kuchukua shughuli muhimu zilizofanywa awali na WHO.
Ameishutumu WHO kwa kuruhusu ugonjwa wa Uviko -19 kushindwa kudhibitika na kupuuzia hatari ya ugonjwa huo, ambao umesababisha vifo vya maelfu ya watu duniani.
Trump ameilaumu China kwa kujaribu kuziba mlipuko huo na kuishtumu WHO kwa kushindwa kuiwajibisha China.
Amelishutumu shirika hilo kwa kuipendelea China, sehemu ya shutuma hizo zikiwa ni kutokana na upingaji wake mkali wa hatua ya Marekani kuwazuia wasafiri kutoka China kuingia nchini humo, akiita ugonjwa huo ni ''virusi vya China.”

Summary:
- WHO will cut salary spending by 25 percent.

Dar es Salaam. As the World Health Organization (WHO) cuts its departments from 76 to 34 and its staff costs by 25 percent after a decline in funding, Tanzania has begun preparing to cope with the move.

WHO took this step about four months after the United States announced its withdrawal from the organisation and the suspension of its funding.

The WHO Director-General, Dr Tedros Ghebreyesus, in his opening speech at the 42nd meeting of the Programme, Budget and Administration Committee of the organisation's Executive Board, held on 14 May 2025, said that the loss of US funding and the decline in official development assistance from some other countries is creating a salary gap of more than US$500 million for the coming two-year period (2026-2027).

"The bitter truth is that we need to reduce salary spending by 25 percent. This does not mean that we will cut 25 percent of staff across the whole organisation.

"But let us not deceive ourselves; we are saying goodbye to a large number of staff with experience, ability and a high level of dedication. This means careers are interrupted and lives disrupted," he said.

He said that in order to help staff during this difficult period, they have set up support systems and are focusing on assisting their mental health and wellbeing.

"We expect that most of the staff reductions will occur at headquarters, although regional offices will also be affected to varying degrees," he said.

He said the prioritisation exercise contributed to the preparation of a new headquarters structure, which he announced last month, reducing the number of senior leaders from 14 to 7 and the number of departments from 76 to 34.

"Regional offices are finalising their plans, which align with headquarters," he said.

Health stakeholders in the country have said that the United States' withdrawal from WHO is a major blow to developing nations, including Tanzania and poor countries.

The President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT), Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, said the matter was expected given the trend of contributions to WHO made by member states.

He said the largest contributor had been the United States for a long time, followed by other bodies from China, European countries and Japan.

The withdrawal has contributed to a reduction in the organisation's operations, so they have taken a decision on how they can work under the present conditions.

"The organisation will be able to run itself without depending on many contributions; it will be able to think of new sources of income to fund its activities without getting stuck," he said, adding:

"We know people have lost jobs; I do not know how many Tanzanians were on the employment list and how many will have been affected by the job cuts. But there are also projects run by WHO that will be affected in one way or another, or will fail to deliver the projects and the expected results for the beneficiaries of that funding. There are effects, but to a large extent they have reduced operating costs."

The Chairman of the Association of Private Health Facilities in Tanzania (Aphfta), Dr Egina Makwabe, said the United States contributes 30 percent of WHO's budget.

"If you look at the vaccine side, at Gavi (the international organisation that produces vaccines), in that plan to provide vaccines to poor countries, the United States was the biggest contributor," he said.

What Tanzania is doing

The Government of Tanzania has said it has sufficient stocks of medicines and vaccines but is coming up with new strategies.

"We have no problem with ARVs; our medicine situation is good and it takes us up to June 2026. When the (Health) Ministry's budget is read you will hear the Government's plans," said the Chief Government Pharmacist, Daudi Msasi, when he spoke to Mwananchi about the strategies in place.

Trump's decision

US President Donald Trump on 20 January 2025 signed an executive order to withdraw from WHO, an organisation founded in 1948 with 193 member states. The United States was among its founders.

Trump said in the order that the United States would stop providing funds, assistance or US Government resources to WHO.

That nation has been providing a great deal of money and health experts through its government institutions.

According to WHO figures, the United States provided Sh3.25 trillion in the period from 2022 to 2023.

That nation has been providing experts and expertise through its institutions such as the Department of Health and Human Services, the US Centers for Disease Control (CDC), the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).

Other major contributors to WHO in 2022-2023 are Germany, Sh2.16 trillion; the Gates Foundation (Sh2.10 trillion); Gavi (Sh1.21 trillion); the European Commission (Sh1.18 trillion); and the United Kingdom and Northern Ireland (Sh1 trillion).

Others are Canada (Sh516.46 billion), Rotary International (Sh448.1 billion), Japan (Sh422.79 billion) and France (Sh407.6 billion).

Earlier, the United States had proposed withdrawing from WHO in 2020 because of the organisation's mishandling of the Covid-19 pandemic that emerged from Wuhan, China, and of other global health problems.

Trump, in his first presidential term, complained that WHO had failed to adopt urgently needed reforms and was unable to demonstrate independence from the inappropriate political influence of the organisation's member states.

"WHO continues to demand unfairly onerous payments from the United States, out of proportion with the assessed payments of other countries. China, with a population of 1.4 billion, has 300 percent of the population of the United States, but contributes nearly 90 percent less to WHO," Trump said.

He said the United States intends to withdraw from WHO, and that a letter of withdrawal to the UN Secretary-General signed on 20 January 2021 revoked the US request of 6 July 2020.

President Trump, in the January 2025 order, said the United States would stop providing funds, assistance or US Government resources to WHO.

He ordered the recall and reassignment of US Government employees or contractors working in any position at WHO.

He said the US Government would seek credible and transparent international partners to take over the essential activities previously carried out by WHO.

He accused WHO of allowing Covid-19 to become uncontrollable and of ignoring the danger of the disease, which has caused the deaths of thousands of people worldwide.

Trump blamed China for trying to cover up the outbreak and accused WHO of failing to hold China accountable.

He accused the organisation of favouring China, part of those accusations stemming from its strong opposition to the US measure barring travellers from China from entering the country, calling the disease the "China virus."
